title: Sell smarter together: timing, groups and written agreements
course_title: Agribusiness and Market Access: Grade, Store and Sell Your Produce for a Better Price

say: Sell smarter together: timing, groups and written agreements.
This is the video for module three of Agribusiness and Market Access.
Just after harvest, almost everyone is selling, so prices for maize, beans and other storable crops tend to be at their lowest. Selling then gives you cash with no storage costs.

panel.heading: Sell at harvest, or store and wait?

say: Months later, in the lean season, prices tend to rise. But the rise is never guaranteed. Storage has real costs and risks, so it is a business decision, not free money.
And a neighbour saying maize will double is a rumour, not evidence.

panel.heading: Sell at harvest, or store and wait?

say: Here is how to decide. These numbers are illustrative.
Selling now at 55,000 naira a bag brings 1,100,000 naira.
To store, she needs hermetic bags for about 50,000 naira. And she must borrow for school fees at 5% a month, which adds 60,000 naira of interest.
Even good storage loses about 2%, leaving 19.6 bags. Add it up and divide. Storage only pays if the price later is clearly above about 61,700 naira a bag.
So Fatima sells 8 bags now to pay the fees without a loan, and stores 12. That removes the interest and halves her risk.
Poor grain should be sold, not stored. Dry maize to about 13% moisture or less first.

panel.heading: Store only dry, clean grain
items: Dry to about 13% or less first
Bags on pallets, away from walls
Seal each layer of hermetic bags
Keep out rats; open bags rarely
Inspect every few weeks

say: Keep bags on wooden pallets, away from walls. Squeeze out the air and tie each inner layer separately.

say: Protect them from rats, open them as little as possible, and check every few weeks for insects, damp or bad smells.

say: Many mills and wholesalers will not buy five or ten bags. They want a full truck. These twelve women have 120 bags together, and a feed mill buys at least 100 per delivery.
At the farm gate they would get 55,000 naira a bag.
The mill pays 66,000. After truck hire of 3,000 a bag and 500 for loading and records, they keep 62,500 naira.

card.title: Twelve women fill one truck
rows: Mill net per bag, after costs

say: That is 75,000 naira more for each woman, and 900,000 naira for the group. It only works because the group checks every member's bags before loading.

say: Put the deal in writing. Name the crop, grade and specification, such as maximum moisture, and the quantity and delivery dates.

panel.heading: What a buyer agreement must say
items: Product, grade and specification
Quantity and delivery dates
Price per kg or a clear formula
Weighing witnessed by a member
Payment, rejection and disputes

say: Fix the price per kilogram or bag, or a clear formula. Agree where the weighing happens, and that a group member watches it.

panel.heading: What a buyer agreement must say
items: Product, grade and specification
Quantity and delivery dates
Price per kg or a clear formula
Weighing witnessed by a member
Payment, rejection and disputes

say: Write how and when payment comes, what happens to rejected bags, and who you go to first if you disagree.

panel.heading: What a buyer agreement must say
items: Product, grade and specification
Quantity and delivery dates
Price per kg or a clear formula
Weighing witnessed by a member
Payment, rejection and disputes

say: Before any negotiation, know your walk-away option, what you will do if this deal fails. If the offer is below it, say no politely.

panel.heading: What a buyer agreement must say
items: Product, grade and specification
Quantity and delivery dates
Price per kg or a clear formula
Weighing witnessed by a member
Payment, rejection and disputes
panel.rule: Know your walk-away price before you negotiate.

say: Be suspicious of any buyer who asks for a registration or processing fee, promises prices far above the market, or will only talk on WhatsApp. Check the company on the CAC public search and ask other farmers.
Pay each woman directly into her own account with a written statement. And never release produce until payment is confirmed in your own account.

panel.heading: Spot fake buyers and protect payment
items: Never pay a fee to be allowed to sell
Doubt prices far above the market
Check CAC registration and references
Pay each member into her own account
Release nothing until money is confirmed

say: To remember. Lean-season prices are never guaranteed. Store only if the likely price is well above your break-even. Bulk with other women to reach bigger buyers. Put every deal in writing. And never pay a fee to sell.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Higher lean-season prices are never guaranteed
Store only above your break-even price
Bulk together to reach bigger buyers
Put every deal in writing
Never pay to sell; confirm payment first

say: Now practise. Calculate your storage break-even. Draft a group selling plan with a one-page agreement. Start your Market Access Project file with your before and after prices, and write a 90-day plan with dated actions.
